title: Research: reversible shared rank-one helper across three calls
body:
## Result

This is a partial local construction for a new helper interface: one clean rank-one product helper shared across three output roles. The exact joint bilinear map has rank four; the reversible schedule counts its cleanup child and reduces the common-factor portion from three rank-one children to two. This is not a selected-provider construction and makes no new conditional-bound claim.

## Evidence

- Seed `5a7846f3daaf14b6c11f30e784e1944a`; track `complex-mechanisms`; task `complex-new-helper-inventory`; base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.
- Map: `F_i=x0*y0+x_i*y_i`, for `i=1,2,3`. Four atoms and a rank-four X-mode flattening prove exact tensor rank four.
- Reversible batch cost: five rank-one child calls per forward triple, versus six separate calls; three additional ADD fanouts; one clean width-one helper slot reused sequentially; one inverse child cleanup already counted.
- Exact selected-profile relaxation first clears the 5% target at 764, 765, or 766 shared products per triple with 0, 1, or 2 further rank-one-equivalent charges. Prior-integer failure and passing-integer bounds are exact.
- The pinned phase-A source stream records scalar gates and climbs, not bilinear operand pairs. It does not establish any selected-provider occurrence.
- `python3 -I -B research/complex-shared-product-triple-seed5a78/verify.py` passes on Python 3.14.7. `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-shared-product-triple-seed5a78 --check-only` passes package metadata and pins.

## Limits

The 5% screen assumes the current coverage law and an average three-call profile. The extra rank-one-equivalent charge is a stress parameter, not a measured physical invoice. Clean-helper availability, operand-triple frequency, hosting and actual frames remain unresolved. No supplier admission or `kappa` change is claimed. The registered replay requests Python 3.12, unavailable locally; hosted CI is separate.
